sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余烬》。

sentences.en: Today we're going to be talking about one of the big isMs.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要探讨的是其中一个巨大的“主义”。

sentences.en: You know, you'll often meet a socialist, an anarchist, even a communiSt. It's very rare that you'll meet somebody who will willingly describe themselves as a fasciSt. So what is
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你经常会遇到社会主义者、无政府主义者，甚至共产主义者。但你很少会遇到有人会心甘情愿地称自己为法西斯主义者。那么，什么是

sentences.en: fascism?
sentences.zh: fascism?

sentences.en: What are its roots?
sentences.zh: 它的根源是什么？

sentences.en: Are all fascist Nazis?
sentences.zh: 所有的法西斯分子都是纳粹吗？

sentences.en: Are any fascist Democrats?
sentences.zh: 有没有法西斯分子是民主党人？

sentences.en: And are all fascists uniquely evil?
sentences.zh: 而且，所有的法西斯分子都具有独特的邪恶属性吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to The Rest is History, the podcast that roams down the dark alleys of political history and shines a torch on the sometimes disturbing ideas that you find in the corners.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史的余烬》，这是一档漫步于政治历史黑暗小巷、并用火炬照亮角落里那些有时令人不安的思想的播客。

sentences.en: I'm Dominic Sandberg and with me is Chief Liberal Elite Investigator Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 我是多米尼克·桑德伯格，坐在我旁边的是首席自由派精英调查员汤姆·霍兰。

sentences.en: Hello
sentences.zh: Hello

sentences.en: Tom, how are you?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你好吗？

sentences.en: Very well, thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 很好，谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: Thanks.

sentences.en: So Tom, we had the most colossal postbag on fascism, as you might expect.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，正如你所预料的那样，我们收到了关于法西斯主义的大量来信。

sentences.en: It's a subject that basically never fails to sell books or, let's hope, podcasts.
sentences.zh: 这是一个基本上永远不会卖不出去书、或者希望也卖不出去播客的主题。

sentences.en: So what have we found?
sentences.zh: 那么我们发现了什么？

sentences.en: Share some of your questions that you've dug up.
sentences.zh: 分享一些你挖掘出来的问题吧。

sentences.en: Well, looking through them, I think that large numbers of them are saying, actually, what is fascism?
sentences.zh: 好的，浏览这些来信，我认为其中很大一部分人实际上都在问：到底什么是法西斯主义？

sentences.en: And there's a question from Kelvin that I think zooms in very well on perhaps what's the core issue.
sentences.zh: 凯尔文提出了一个问题，我认为它非常好地切中了核心问题所在。

sentences.en: He asks, is there an actual historical definition of fascism?
sentences.zh: 他问，法西斯主义是否存在一个实际的历史定义？

sentences.en: Or is it more of a I know it when I see it type of scenario?
sentences.zh: 还是更偏向于“我一眼就能认出来”的那种情况？

sentences.en: And then he adds, for instance, could retrospectively the Spartans of ancient Greece count?
sentences.zh: 然后他补充说，比如，回过头来看，古希腊的斯巴达人算不算？

sentences.en: So I think that at the heart, is fascism something that can be abstracted from history?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，归根结底，法西斯主义是一种可以从历史中抽象出来的东西吗？

sentences.en: Is it something that can describe maybe an attitude towards authoritarianism or racism or whatever that is a constant throughout history?
sentences.zh: 它是一种可以用来描述对威权主义、种族主义等某种贯穿历史始终的态度的东西吗？

sentences.en: Or is it something that is rooted in very specific cultural, political, economic circumstances?
sentences.zh: 还是说它根植于非常特定的文化、政治和经济环境中？

sentences.en: And personally, I would go for the latter.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我会选择后者。

sentences.en: I don't know how you feel.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你怎么看。

sentences.en: You're the modern historian.
sentences.zh: 你可是现代史学家。

sentences.en: What's your take on that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: I absolutely would go for the latter.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会选择后者。

sentences.en: I would say it is, people use fascists now to mean evil, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我会说，人们现在用“法西斯”来指代邪恶，对吧？

sentences.en: Which I think is sort of wrong.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这某种程度上是错的。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not saying fascists weren't evil, but it's not, to use it as a moral shorthand, I think is wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我并不是说法西斯分子不邪恶，但把它当作一种道德简写来用，我认为是不对的。

sentences.en: I think it's, fascism was rooted in a very specific time and place in the decades after the First World War.
sentences.zh: 我认为，法西斯主义根植于第一次世界大战后几十年的一个非常特定的时间和地点。

sentences.en: I think the First World War was absolutely central to fascism.
sentences.zh: 我认为第一次世界大战对法西斯主义至关重要。

sentences.en: And, you know, historians, to answer Kelvin's question, historians have spent, you know, enormous amounts of time and ink debating what fascism is.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，为了回答凯尔文的问题，历史学家们花了大量的时间和笔墨来争论什么是法西斯主义。

sentences.en: And they come back to, by and large, people like Robert Paxton and Roger Griffin, these sort of landmark historians of fascism, they come back to the same things.
sentences.zh: 他们最终回归到——大体上，像罗伯特·帕克斯顿和罗杰·格里芬这样法西斯主义研究的里程碑式历史学家——他们都回归到了相同的核心。

sentences.en: So it's rooted in a nation that has a sense of victimhood and humiliation, and often through war.
sentences.zh: 所以它根植于一个具有受害者情结和屈辱感的国家，而且往往是通过战争。

sentences.en: And it strives for a kind of national rebirth.
sentences.zh: 它争取一种国家的涅槃重生。

sentences.en: It rejects democracy.
sentences.zh: 它排斥民主。

sentences.en: It defines itself against communism.
sentences.zh: 它通过与共产主义对立来定义自己。

sentences.en: It argues that there's room for a kind of revolutionary movement that will remake the nation and will restore its lost kind of virility,
sentences.zh: 它认为存在这样一种革命运动的空间，能够重塑国家、恢复其失去的阳刚之气，

sentences.en: and it's lost pride, and create new men, in fact, will create a new kind of a new kind of human being through speed and spectacle and technology and violence.
sentences.zh: 以及失去的尊严，并创造出新人——事实上，是通过速度、奇观、技术和暴力，创造出一种全新的人类。

sentences.en: And violence is always at the core of it.
sentences.zh: 而暴力始终是其核心。

sentences.en: And you can see, I think, now maybe you'll disagree with me about this, Tom, but I think
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，我想，也许你会不同意我的看法，汤姆，但我认为

sentences.en: although you can see elements of all those things in earlier movements, and some of them are kind of
sentences.zh: 尽管你可以在早期的运动中看到所有这些要素的影子，并且其中一些某种程度上是

sentences.en: timeless, the formula is very specific and is rooted in that experience of the First World War and the sort of sense of humiliation afterwards.
sentences.zh: 永恒的，但这个公式非常具体，并且深深根植于第一次世界大战的经历以及战后那种屈辱感之中。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, my take on it is perhaps a kind of slightly strange one, because I've never studied fascism.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的看法可能有点奇怪，因为我从未研究过法西斯主义。

sentences.en: I never did it at school, never did it at university.
sentences.zh: 我上学时没学过，在大学里也没学过。

sentences.en: And the only time I've written about it was in the context of writing about Christianity.
sentences.zh: 我唯一一次写到它是在探讨基督教的语境下。

sentences.en: And it seems to me that fascism is the most profoundly revolutionary movement that Europe has
sentences.zh: 在我看来，法西斯主义是欧洲见证过的最具颠覆性的革命运动，

sentences.en: witnessed, because it represents an overturning not just of institutional Christian norms, as the
sentences.zh: 因为它代表的不仅是对体制化基督教规范的推翻（正如法国大革命和俄国大革命所做的那样），而且是对自由主义后基督教所继承的基督教核心基本价值的攻击。

sentences.en: French Revolution and the Russian Revolution did, but an attack on some of the core fundamental values of Christianity that liberal post-Christianity has inherited.
sentences.zh: 我特别想指出其中两点。

sentences.en: And I would fix on two in particular.
sentences.zh: 在基督教的核心，正如十字架上的基督形象所体现的那样，有一种理念认为苦难本身具有某种美德，即首要的将成为末后的，末后的将成为首要的。

sentences.en: At the heart of Christianity, as evinced by the image of Christ on the cross, is the idea that there
sentences.zh: 纳粹显然不同意这一点，墨索里尼领导下的法西斯分子也不同意。

sentences.en: is a kind of a virtue in victimhood, that those who are the first shall be last, the last shall be firSt.
sentences.zh: 另一个基督教核心理念是存在普遍的人类尊严，所有人都是按神的形象平等创造的。

sentences.en: The Nazis obviously do not agree with that, neither do the fascists under Mussolini.
sentences.zh: 正如圣保罗所说，不再有希腊人与犹太人之分。

sentences.en: The other core Christian idea is that there is a universal human dignity, that all human beings are created equally in the image of God.
sentences.zh: 现在很显然，尤其是纳粹非常热衷于这样一种观点，即犹太人和希腊人有着根本的区别和界限。

sentences.en: And that, as St. Paul puts it, there is no dual Greek.
sentences.zh: 我认为根本上，你知道的，我们刚才已经谈到纳粹和法西斯是邪恶的。

sentences.en: Now, obviously, the Nazis in particular are very, very keen on the idea that Jews and Greeks are fundamentally separate and distinct.
sentences.zh: 这当然本质上是一种基督教式的分类。

sentences.en: And I think that fundamentally, you know, we've already talked about Nazis and fascists being evil.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们之所以如此轻易地这样做，恰恰是因为法西斯分子和纳粹分子猛烈抨击了我们今天仍然拥有的核心道德价值，以至于我认为在某种程度上，我们不再……自二次世界大战以来，体制化基督教急剧衰落的原因之一，某种意义上是因为纳粹替我们把这活儿干了。

sentences.en: That, of course, is essentially a kind of Christian categorisation.
sentences.zh: 希特勒在某种意义上就是撒旦。

sentences.en: And I think that the reason that we do that so readily is precisely the fact that the
sentences.zh: 纳粹就是恶魔。

sentences.en: fascists and the Nazis in particular assaulted the core moral values of what, the core moral values
sentences.zh: 奥斯威辛就是地狱。

sentences.en: that we still have today, to the degree that I think that, to an extent, we no longer, one of the
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们想知道——你知道的，在以前的几代人中，如果我们想知道

sentences.en: reasons that institutional Christianity has declined so profoundly since the Second World War is that, in a sense, the Nazis do the job for us.
sentences.zh: 什么是正确的事，什么是善，什么是道德上的善，我们会说，耶稣会怎么做？

sentences.en: Hitler, in a sense, is Satan.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，希特勒就是撒旦。

sentences.en: The Nazis are the demons.
sentences.zh: 纳粹就是恶魔。

sentences.en: The Auschwitz is hell.
sentences.zh: 奥斯威辛就是地狱。

sentences.en: And so if we want to know, you know, in previous generations, if we wanted to know
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们想知道，你知道的，在以前的世代，如果我们想知道

sentences.en: what the right thing is, what is good, what is morally good, we would say, what would Jesus do?
sentences.zh: 什么是正确的事，什么是善，什么是道德上的善，我们会说，耶稣会怎么做？

sentences.en: And do it.
sentences.zh: 把它做了。

sentences.en: Now we tend to ask, what would Hitler do?
sentences.zh: 现在我们往往会问：希特勒会怎么做？

sentences.en: And do the opposite.
sentences.zh: 然后反其道而行之。

sentences.en: So it's become a sort of moral yardstick, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这已经变成了一种某种意义上的道德标尺，对吧？

sentences.en: But let me drag you for a second away from
sentences.zh: 但请允许我稍微把话题从

sentences.en: Christianity and towards the Romans, which is one of your other big fields.
sentences.zh: 基督教拉开，转向罗马人，这也是你们的另一个主要研究领域。

sentences.en: So the first fascists, I mean, there's lots of questions about the origins of fascism, but the first really successful fascist party was obviously in Italy.
sentences.zh: 所以最早的法西斯分子，我是说，关于法西斯主义的起源有很多问题，但第一个真正成功的法西斯政党显然在意大利。

sentences.en: And it was in Italy, and a Mussolini, that you had the invention of the term fascism and the fascist iconography.
sentences.zh: 正是在意大利，在墨索里尼的领导下，你们才有了“法西斯主义”这个词以及法西斯标志的发明。

sentences.en: And they were looking back straight away to the Romans.
sentences.zh: 而且他们立刻把目光投向了罗马人。

sentences.en: And what is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, the fasces, I think, I assume that's the right pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 我是说，法西斯（fasces）这个词，我想，我猜这是正确的发音。

sentences.en: What's all that about?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: What are those things?
sentences.zh: 那些东西是什么？

sentences.en: So the idea of the fasces is that if you bump, they're rods, birching rods.
sentences.zh: 所以法西斯的理念是，如果你碰一下，它们是棍子，惩戒棒。

sentences.en: And in the Roman Republic, they are emblems of a magistrate's, right to beat those who oppose him.
sentences.zh: 在罗马共和国，它们是地方长官有权鞭打反对者权力的象征。

sentences.en: And they're carried on the shoulders of officials called lictors who march around with the magistrate.
sentences.zh: 它们由被称为刀斧手的官员扛在肩上，这些官员跟随地方长官四处行进。

sentences.en: And the symbolism of the fasces is that you can break one rod, but if they're bundled up, you can't.
sentences.zh: 法西斯的象征意义在于，你可以折断一根棍子，但如果它们被捆扎在一起，你就折不断。

sentences.en: And so the appeal of that to Mussolini is evident that if you can join the entire nation together, then it cannot possibly be broken.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对墨索里尼的吸引力是显而易见的：如果你能把整个国家凝聚在一起，那么它就绝不可能被折断。

sentences.en: But of course, the fact that it is redolent of ancient Rome, and for Mussolini, of course, the Roman Empire,
sentences.zh: 但当然，它让人联想到古代罗马，对墨索里尼来说，当然还有罗马帝国，

sentences.en: which governs the whole Mediterranean, is a reminder of a kind of state of lost Italian greatness, that is absolutely kind of fundamental to the appeal.
sentences.zh: 它统治着整个地中海，这唤起了一种对意大利失去的伟大状态的记忆，这绝对是其吸引力的核心所在。

sentences.en: And it's kind of the strangeness of it is, I mean, as you mentioned in your opening, is that fascists are simultaneously drawn to the very ancient, but also to the modern.
sentences.zh: 这种现象有些奇特之处，就像你在开场时提到的那样，法西斯分子一方面被极度古老的事物所吸引，另一方面又被现代事物所吸引。

sentences.en: And it's that fusion of iconography drawn from ancient Rome with planes and cars and tanks and everything that is modern, that I think is pretty fundamental to the
sentences.zh: 正是这种将源自古罗马的标志与飞机、汽车、坦克以及所有现代事物融合在一起的东西，我认为这是法西斯主义定义的

sentences.en: definition of fascism.
sentences.zh: 核心所在。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd agree with that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我同意这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, Prashant Rao asks this question, who was the first recorded fascist?
sentences.zh: 我是说，普拉尚特·拉奥提出了这样一个问题：谁是有记载以来的第一个法西斯分子？

sentences.en: And my answer to that, I mean, maybe you'll delve further back into history, but my answer to
sentences.zh: 而我的回答是——也许你会更深入地探究历史——但我的回答是

sentences.en: that would be, Mussolini is obviously the first sort of fascist, successful fascist leader.
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼显然是那种最初的法西斯分子，是成功的法西斯领导人。

sentences.en: He is the person who sort of turns fascism into an international brand, and who turns it into a governing creed rather than a sort of oppositional one.
sentences.zh: 他是将法西斯主义变成一个国际品牌，并将其变成一种统治信条，而不仅仅是一种对立信条的人。

sentences.en: I mean, he had predecessors, you'll maybe know this brilliant book, The Pike, by Lucy, who's Hallett, about Gabriele D'Annunzio.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他有前任，你可能知道露西·休斯-哈莱特写的那本关于加布里埃尔·邓邓齐奥的精彩著作《长矛》（The Pike）。

sentences.en: Now, D'Annunzio was this poet, but he was also a kind of playboy and a celebrity and an aviator.
sentences.zh: 邓邓齐奥不仅是一位诗人，也是一位花花公子、名人和飞行员。

sentences.en: He had led the campaign to get Italy into the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他曾领导让意大利加入第一次世界大战的运动。

sentences.en: And D'Annunzio anticipated all the themes that we associate with Mussolini about speed, excitement, virility, violence, blood, a sort of rebirth of
sentences.zh: 邓邓齐奥预示了所有我们与墨索里尼联系在一起的主题：速度、兴奋、阳刚之气、暴力、血性、一种意大利的某种重生，

sentences.en: Italy, which he saw as this failing state, a new state, but a failing state through war.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，意大利是一个失败的国家，是一个新国家，但却通过战争走向失败的国家。

sentences.en: And I think actually before Mussolini, I think a lot of people, historians would buy this.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，在墨索里尼之前，我想很多人，历史学家都会认同这一点。

sentences.en: D'Annunzio is the kind of John the Baptist, to use your Christian sort of formula.
sentences.zh: 借用你们基督教的说法，邓邓齐奥就像是施洗约翰。

sentences.en: He is John the Baptist to Mussolini's
sentences.zh: 他是墨索里尼的施洗约翰，而墨索里尼则是……

sentences.en: Messiah.
sentences.zh: Messiah.

sentences.en: And in the wake of the First World War, he sets up a kind of proto-fascist state in
sentences.zh: 在第一次世界大战之后，他在里耶卡建立了一种原初法西斯国家。

sentences.en: Fumé, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 抽烟的，对吧？

sentences.en: He does, in what's now Rijeka.
sentences.zh: 他的确这么做了，就在现在的里耶卡。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: Yes.

sentences.en: I mean, and he introduces an awful lot of what will become iconically fascist, including the Roman salute, including the black shirts, including addresses from balconies.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他引入了大量后来成为法西斯标志性的东西，包括罗马礼、黑衫军以及在阳台上发表讲话。

sentences.en: He was very keen on feeding castor oil to his enemies, which was something that Mussolini was so big on as well.
sentences.zh: 他非常热衷于给敌人喂蓖麻油，这也是墨索里尼非常热衷的事情。

sentences.en: So I guess, yeah, D'Annunzio is kind of, but he's, as you say, the kind of the John the Baptist figure.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，是的，邓邓齐奥有点像，但正如你所说，他是那种施洗约翰式的人物。

sentences.en: But Mussolini really is the, I mean, he's the guy who blazes the path, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但墨索里尼才是真正的，我是说，他才是那个开辟道路的人，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, well, he is.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，他是。

sentences.en: But so Kelvin, you mentioned in Kelvin's question,
sentences.zh: 但是凯尔文，你在凯尔文的问题中提到了……

sentences.en: Kelvin asked about the Spartans.
sentences.zh: 凯尔文问到了斯巴达人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.
